allies.rationale_text: Cognitive-load-theory gives boundaries a concrete limit condition by showing why genuinely manageable chunks matter for real comprehension and execution.
allies.source_quote: the boundary of limited working memory
allies.affinity_rationale: Directly informs the boundary mechanism — 'the boundary of limited working memory informs the effective strategy of Scaffolding' — CLT provides the empirical justification for why boundaries must respect cognitive capacity.
allies.activation_condition: When scope boundaries need to be sized to respect working memory limits rather than set by arbitrary project convention or stakeholder ambition

allies.rationale_text: Decomposition helps boundaries divide the work cleanly so scope becomes usable rather than abstract.
allies.affinity_rationale: Practical structuring tool — 'Logical decompositions help structure problems' — turns abstract boundary definitions into usable work breakdown but is a tool applied within boundaries rather than the mechanism that creates them.
allies.activation_condition: When defined scope boundaries need to be broken into logical, non-overlapping subcomponents that can be independently addressed

allies.rationale_text: Prioritization sharpens boundaries by forcing choices about what deserves attention now and what belongs outside the active frame.
allies.source_quote: defining limits before engaging in complex tasks
allies.affinity_rationale: Sharpens boundary selection — 'defining limits before engaging in complex tasks' — forces the choice of what belongs inside the active frame, but operates as boundary sharpener rather than boundary justifier.
allies.activation_condition: When multiple concerns compete for inclusion within the active boundary and explicit ranking is needed to decide what stays inside versus outside the frame

antagonists.rationale_text: Theory-induced-blindness undermines boundaries when a familiar frame dictates the scope instead of the real objective and evidence landscape.
antagonists.source_quote: apply an existing model ... to a situation where it doesn't fit
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Directly corrupts boundary placement — described as 'a direct challenge to the wise use of boundaries' where a familiar model dictates scope instead of the real objective and evidence landscape.
antagonists.activation_condition: When scope boundaries are being drawn by a familiar theoretical framework rather than derived from the actual problem structure and available evidence

structured_tensions.tension_text: Boundaries conflicts with systems-thinking when artificially narrow system boundaries hide feedback loops and interdependencies that cross the defined perimeter.
structured_tensions.source_quote: boundaries conflicts with systems-thinking (systems thinking) when artificially narrow system boundaries hide feedback loops and interdependencies that cross the defined perimeter.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Boundaries conflicts with optionality when prematurely fixed boundaries close off adjacent opportunities that emerge only through exploratory scope expansion.
structured_tensions.source_quote: boundaries conflicts with optionality (optionality) when prematurely fixed boundaries close off adjacent opportunities that emerge only through exploratory scope expansion.
